title: Scalar change and the normalized open adjunct of inverse exchange
statement:
Use Grothendieck topoi with fixed small-site presentations [def-weil-pbc-topos] and constant sheaves of commutative rings. A morphism of topoi $v:T\to W$ means an adjunction $v^{-1}\dashv v_*$ with $v^{-1}$ preserving finite limits. For a ring $R$, write $D_R(T)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $L_{v,R}=v^{-1}$ and $R_{v,R}=Rv_*$, with their derived adjunction and counit $\varepsilon_{v,R}$. An open embedding means the inclusion of the slice topos of a subterminal object; its exact extension by zero $I_{j,R}$ is left adjoint to $L_{j,R}$, fully faithful, with unit $\eta_{j,R}:1\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{j,R}I_{j,R}$. All equations below insert the canonical inverse-image and direct-image compositors. For a unital ring map $A\to B$ put $S_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and let $U_T:D_B(T)\to D_A(T)$ be exact restriction of scalars. Use the canonical tensor/pullback comparison $\lambda_v:L_{v,B}S_W\xrightarrow{\sim}S_TL_{v,A}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Define $\chi_v:S_WR_{v,A}\to R_{v,B}S_T$ as the adjoint transpose of $S_T(\varepsilon_{v,A})\lambda_v$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and, for an open embedding $j:V\hookrightarrow T$, $\beta_j:S_TI_{j,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}I_{j,B}S_V$ as the balancing map induced by tensoring sections on the open and the zero map on its complement. Let $b:V\hookrightarrow T$, $i:Y\hookrightarrow Z$, $r:V\to Y$, and $p:T\to Z$ form a Cartesian square, $pb=ir$. For $R=A,B$ let
$$E_R:L_{i,R}R_{p,R}\longrightarrow R_{r,R}L_{b,R}$$
be the adjunction-mate exchange of the inverse-image square. Assume that $E_RI_{b,R}$ is invertible on the inputs in question. Put
$$t_R=R_{r,R}(\eta_{b,R}^{-1})\,E_RI_{b,R}:L_{i,R}R_{p,R}I_{b,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{r,R}$$
and define $\gamma_R:I_{i,R}R_{r,R}\to R_{p,R}I_{b,R}$ as the $I_{i,R}\dashv L_{i,R}$ adjunct of $t_R^{-1}$. Thus the normalization is $t_R L_{i,R}(\gamma_R)\eta_{i,R,R_{r,R}(-)}=1$.
For any $N\in D_A(T)$ the specified maps satisfy
$$\chi_{r,L_{b,A}N}\,S_Y(E_{A,N})\,\lambda_{i,R_{p,A}N}
=R_{r,B}(\lambda_{b,N})\,E_{B,S_TN}\,L_{i,B}(\chi_{p,N}).$$
For any $M\in D_A(V)$ on which both $t_A$ and $t_B$ are invertible, with the $B$-input $S_VM$, they satisfy the following equality of actual $B$-linear morphisms:
$$R_{p,B}(\beta_{b,M})\,\chi_{p,I_{b,A}M}\,S_Z(\gamma_{A,M})
=\gamma_{B,S_VM}\,I_{i,B}(\chi_{r,M})\,\beta_{i,R_{r,A}M}.$$
The source is $S_ZI_{i,A}R_{r,A}M$ and the target is $R_{p,B}I_{b,B}S_VM$. Both identities are natural. They require no invertibility of $\chi_p$, $\chi_r$ or $\gamma_R$. When the categories are restricted to $D^+$, require all displayed inputs and their scalar extensions to belong to $D^+$. There is no properness, finite-ring or Noetherian hypothesis. In particular the statement concerns the normalization of the inverse-exchange adjunct, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism with the same endpoints.

proof.text: Prove the ordinary coefficient/inverse-image cube directly from the specified ScalarPure and SquarePure equations. Scalar-extension maps are determined after precomposition with m ↦ 1 ⊗ m, by the sheafified tensor hom equivalence. The two geometric insertions for constant coefficients are isomorphisms: their ring maps are components of the constant-ring isomorphism, and scalar extension along a ring isomorphism is an equivalence. Thus equality can be tested on the iterated inverse-image insertion. Naturality moves the scalar comparison through the second geometric insertion. The two ScalarPure equations along each route, the two SquarePure equations, and naturality of the inverse-image square identify the results. Lift this equality degreewise to cochain maps. To prove the derived cube, use flat-term K-flat resolutions and localization natural-transformation extensionality. Postcompose with the invertible composite of the two exact pullback comparisons and scalar-extension comparison. Apply the given SquareResolving and ScalarResolving equations, and naturality of the cochain comparisons, along both routes. Pullback and scalar extension preserve the flat-term K-flat class, so every resolving equation applies. The remaining equality is Q applied to the ordinary cochain cube. Cancel the invertible computation map and descend from resolutions to all derived objects.

proof.text:
The definitions of $\chi_v$ and $E_R$, together with the counit-transpose identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], give
$$\varepsilon_{v,B,S_TK}\,L_{v,B}(\chi_{v,K})=S_T(\varepsilon_{v,A,K})\,\lambda_{v,R_{v,A}K},\qquad
\varepsilon_{r,R,L_{b,R}N}\,L_{r,R}(E_{R,N})=L_{b,R}(\varepsilon_{p,R,N})\,\theta_{R,R_{p,R}N}.\tag{2}$$
These are equations for the actual maps: [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] specifies each mate by its counit transpose, including for the inverse-image square. In particular we can compare maps into $R_{r,B}$ by comparing their transposes under $L_{r,B}\dashv R_{r,B}$.

proof.text: Transpose the exchange/scalar identity under L_rB ⊣ R_rB. Use the counit equations for the actual chi and exchange mates. Naturality of lambda_r moves the A-exchange through lambda_r. On the other side, naturality of the B-counit moves lambda_b, and naturality of the B-square moves chi_p. Its counit equation and naturality of lambda_b leave the derived inverse-image scalar cube at R_pA N, followed by S_V L_bA of the A-counit. The cube identifies the transposes, and the adjunction bijection identifies the original morphisms. No scalar/direct-image comparison is inverted.

proof.text: Derive the open-unit equation directly from betaB_mate and betaI_mate. For either open adjunction apply Mathlib unit_mateEquiv to beta inverse and replace its mate by lambda inverse using the supplied equality. Postcompose with lambda to obtain unit_B ≫ L_B(beta inverse) ≫ lambda = S(unit_A). Precompose with L_B(beta), then cancel the invertible unit_B and use functoriality on unit_A and its inverse. This gives L_B(beta) ≫ inverse(unit_B) = lambda ≫ S(inverse(unit_A)). No separate open-subtopos scalar/unit theorem is needed.

proof.text: Precompose the claimed gamma/scalar identity with betaI inverse and transpose under I_iB ⊣ L_iB. Postcompose both transposes with t_B, which is invertible on the stated input. The t-compatibility equation, naturality of lambda_i for gamma_A, and the open-unit equation for i reduce the first transpose to chi_r, using the defining normalization of gamma_A. Naturality of the B-open unit and the defining normalization of gamma_B reduce the second to chi_r. Cancel t_B, apply the adjunction bijection, and cancel betaI inverse. Gamma normalization itself is the homEquiv right-inverse equation followed by cancellation of t and its inverse.

proof.text: Naturality of exchange and of the open unit gives the naturality square for t. On inputs where both components of t are invertible, multiply by their inverses to obtain the naturality square for inverse t. Transpose under the open adjunction to prove naturality of gamma. All equalities are actual morphism equalities in the coefficient-module derived categories. They restrict to the full bounded-below subcategories whenever all displayed objects belong there. No properness, coefficient finiteness, Noetherianity, or scalar flatness is used.
